'''Microsoft Dynamics 365''' is a set of enterprise accounting and sales software products.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/microsoft-readies-combined-crm-erp-dynamics-365-cloud-bundle/|title=Microsoft readies combined CRM, ERP Dynamics 365 cloud bundle|first=Mary Jo|last=Foley|date=July 6, 2016|website=ZDNet}}</ref> Its flagship product, Dynamics GP, was released in 1981.{{Citation needed |date=November 2025}}

== Applications==
Microsoft Dynamics 365 largely consists of products developed by companies that Microsoft acquired: Dynamics GP (formerly [[Great Plains Software]]), Dynamics NAV (formerly Navision; now forked into Dynamics 365 Business Central), Dynamics SL (formerly Solomon), and Dynamics AX (formerly Axapta; now forked into Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations).{{Citation needed |date=November 2025}} The various products are aimed at different market segments, ranging from small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) to large organizations with multi-language, currency, and legal entity capability.{{Citation needed |date=November 2025}} In recent years{{When |date=November 2025}} Microsoft Dynamics ERP has focused its marketing and development on [[software as a service]] (SaaS) products.{{Citation needed |date=November 2025}}

Microsoft Dynamics 365 contains more than 15 applications:<ref>[https://dynamics.microsoft.com/en-us/ "Microsoft Dynamics 365"] website</ref>

*[[Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales]]{{snd}}Sales Leaders, Sales Operations
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer data platform{{snd}}Customer Insights
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer data platform{{snd}}Customer Voice
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service{{snd}}Customer Service Leaders, Customer Service Operations
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service{{snd}}Field Service Leaders, Field Service Operations
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Remote Assist
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Human Resources{{snd}}Attract, Onboard, Core HR
*[[#Finance|Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations]]{{snd}}Finance Leaders, Operation Leaders
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management{{snd}}Streamline planning, production, stock, warehouse, and transportation
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Intelligent Order Management
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Commerce
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Marketing{{snd}}Adobe Marketing Cloud, Dynamics 365 for Marketing
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Artificial Intelligence{{snd}}AI for Sales, AI for Customer Service, AI for Market Insight
*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Mixed Reality{{snd}}Remote Assist, Layout, Guides
*[[Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central]]{{snd}}ERP for SMBs

== Microsoft Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations ==
'''Microsoft Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations''' Enterprise Edition (formerly [[Microsoft Dynamics AX]]) {{En dash}} ERP and CRM [[software-as-a-service]] product meant for mid-sized and large enterprises. Integrating both Dynamics AX and Dynamics CRM features, consisting of the following modules: for Financials and Operations, for Sales Enterprise, for Marketing, for Customer Service, for Field Service, for Project Service Automation. It is designed to be easily connected with [[Office 365]] and [[Microsoft Power BI]].

===Microsoft Dynamics ax===
'''Microsoft Dynamics AX''' was one of [[Microsoft]]'s Enterprise resource planning (ERP) software products. In 2018, its thick-client interface was removed and the web product was rebranded as ''Microsoft Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations'' as a part of the Dynamics 365 suite. MDCC or Microsoft Development Center [[Copenhagen]] was once the primary development center for Dynamics AX.<ref>[http://www.microsoft.com/danmark/om/mdcc/default.mspx "Microsoft Development Center Copenhagen"] ''Microsoft website''</ref> Microsoft Dynamics AX contained 19 core modules:<ref>[http://www.microsoft.com/dynamics/AX/product/editionsandfeatures.mspx "Microsoft Dynamics AX Business Ready Licensing editions"] ''Microsoft website''</ref>

====Traditional core (since axapta 2.5)====
*[[General ledger]] – ledger, sales tax, currency, and fixed assets features
*Bank management – receives and pays cash
*[[Customer relationship management]] (CRM) – business relations contact and maintenance (customers, vendors, and leads)
*[[Accounts receivable]] – order entry, shipping, and invoicing
*[[Accounts payable]] – purchase orders, goods received into inventory
*Inventory management – inventory management and valuation<ref>[http://www.dynamicsaxtraining.com/dynamics-ax-trade-and-logistics-training/training-introduction "Inventory management in Dynamics AX"] ''Dynamics AX Training''</ref>
*[[Master planning (resources)]] – purchase and [[production planning]]
*Production – bills of materials, manufacturing tracking
* Store, manage, and interpret data.<ref>https://www.jetglobal.com/blog/microsoft-dynamics-ax-feature-list/ Microsoft Dynamics AX Feature List</ref>

====Extended core====
The following modules are part of the core of AX 2009 (AX 5.0) and available on a per-license basis in AX 4.0:
*[[Shop floor control]]
*[[Cost accounting]]
*[[Balanced scorecard]]s
*[[Service management]]
*[[Expense management]]
*[[Payroll]] management<ref>[http://www.microsoft.com/dynamics/ax/product/MicrosoftDynamicsAX_Payroll_WhitePaper.mspx "Payroll Management – Microsoft Dynamics AX"] ''Microsoft website''</ref>
* Environmental management<ref>[http://www.microsoft.com/environment/dynamics.aspx "The Environmental Sustainability Dashboard"] ''Microsoft website''</ref>

{{redirect|MorphX|the video game|MorphX (video game)}}
X++ integrates SQL queries into standard Java-style code.

====Presence on the internet====
Information about Axapta prior to the Microsoft purchase was available on {{Not a typo|technet.navision.com}}, a proprietary web-based newsgroup,<!--call it a plain newsgroup if it's NNTP--> which grew to a considerable number of members and posts before the Microsoft purchase in 2002.

After Microsoft incorporated Axapta into their Business Solution suite, they transferred the newsgroup's content to the Microsoft Business Solutions newsgroup.<ref>[http://www.microsoft.com/dynamics/AX/community.mspx "Microsoft Dynamics AX Community"] ''Microsoft website''</ref> The oldest Axapta Technet post that can be found dates to August 2000.<ref>{{cite newsgroup |title=26.1 Any input to the benchmarking tool in Damgaard Axapta?? |date=2000-08-04 |url=http://www.microsoft.com/Businesssolutions/Community/NewsGroups/dgbrowser/en-us/default.mspx?dg=microsoft.public.axapta&tid=77de7d66-9415-49f1-8830-508e28245c07&cat=&lang=en&cr=US&sloc=en-us&p=1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024001119/http://community.dynamics.com/product/ax/f/33.aspx |archive-date=2012-10-24 }} [http://techstack.com/forum/microsoft-dynamics-ax/54384-26-1-any-input-benchmarking-tool-damgaard-axapta.html Alt URL] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250906182321/https://techstack.com/forum/microsoft-dynamics-ax/54384-26-1-any-input-benchmarking-tool-damgaard-axapta.html |date=2025-09-06 }}</ref>

'''Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central''' (formerly ''Microsoft Dynamics NAV'') {{En dash}} ERP and CRM [[software-as-a-service]] product meant for small and mid-sized businesses. Integrating both Dynamics NAV and Dynamics CRM features, consisting of the following modules: for Financials and Operations, for Sales Professionals, for Marketing. Easily connected with [[Office 365]] and [[Microsoft Power BI]].

*Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement (formerly Microsoft CRM). Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement contains modules to interact with customers: Marketing, Sales, Customer Service, Field Service. The Customer Service is a module used to automate customer service processes providing performance data reports and dashboards.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scnsoft.com/microsoft-dynamics-365/customer-service|title=Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service – ScienceSoft}}</ref>

=== Online and on-premises deployment===
The Dynamics 365 Business Central system comes in both an online hosted ([[Software as a Service|SaaS]]) version and an on-premises version for manual deployment and administration.

Some features, such as integration with other online Microsoft services, are not available in the on-premises version and only in the online edition.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Features not implemented in on-premises deployments – Business Central|url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/features-not-implemented-on-premises|access-date=2022-02-24|website=docs.microsoft.com|language=en-us}}</ref>

=== Localization===
As an international ERP system, Business Central is available with 24 official [[Internationalization and localization|localizations]] to work with the local features and requirements of various countries. Local partners provide an additional 47 localizations.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Country/region availability and supported languages – Business Central|url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/compliance/apptest-countries-and-translations|access-date=2022-02-24|website=docs.microsoft.com|language=en-us}}</ref>

The system is compliant with various internal financial standards to meet local requirements, such as [[GDPR]], [[International Financial Reporting Standards|IAS/IFRS]] and [[Sarbanes–Oxley Act|SOX]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Application Compliance – Business Central|url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/compliance/compliance-application-compliance|access-date=2022-02-24|website=docs.microsoft.com|language=en-us}}</ref>

=== Editions and licensing===
There are two editions of Business Central, '''Essentials''' and '''Premium'''. Essentials covers [[Financial accounting|Finance]], Sales, Marketing, Purchasing, Inventory, [[Warehouse management system|Warehousing]], and Project Management. Premium includes all of Essentials functionality plus [[Service Management]] and Manufacturing features.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Corporation|first=Microsoft|title=Business Central Pricing {{!}} Microsoft Dynamics 365|url=https://dynamics.microsoft.com/en-us/business-central/pricing/|access-date=2022-02-24|website=dynamics.microsoft.com|language=en}}</ref>

With the arrival of NAV 2013, Microsoft introduced a new licensing model that operated on a [[concurrent user]] basis. With this model, user licenses were of two types: A full user or a limited user. The full user has access to the entire system, whereas the limited user only has read access to the system and limited write access.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/jj551750%28v=nav.71%29.aspx|title=License Types|access-date=March 3, 2014|publisher=MSDN}}</ref> 

From the Business Central rebrand launch, the licensing model changed to a [[per-seat license]] model with a 3x concurrent seat multiplier added to any existing perpetual licenses from previous Dynamics NAV versions. Customers with a Dynamics NAV Extended Pack license were moved to the Premium edition.

=== Value-Added Resellers (VARs) ===
Business Central is primarily distributed and implemented through Microsoft’s global network of Value-Added Resellers (VARs) and Independent Software Vendors (ISVs). VARs provide services such as consulting, implementation, customization, integration, training, and ongoing support. Because Business Central is highly extensible, VARs frequently tailor deployments to meet the specific requirements of industries such as manufacturing, distribution, retail, professional services, and field service.<ref name="MSDocs">{{cite web |title=Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central Documentation |url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/ |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=2025-02-01}}</ref>

ISVs supplement the core product by offering add-on applications and extensions through Microsoft AppSource. These extensions expand Business Central’s capabilities in areas such as reporting, payroll, manufacturing execution, commerce, document management, and integrations with third-party systems. Together, VARs and ISVs enable Business Central to support a wide range of industry and regional scenarios while maintaining a standardized cloud platform.<ref name="AppSource">{{cite web |title=Microsoft AppSource |url=https://appsource.microsoft.com |publisher=Microsoft |access-date=2025-02-01}}</ref>

Sabre Limited also offers training, support, and industry-specific consulting services.<ref>{{cite web |title=Business Central for Manufacturing |url=https://www.sabrelimited.com |publisher=Sabre Limited |access-date=2025-02-01}}</ref>

* '''Innovia Consulting''' – A long-established Business Central/NAV partner specializing in cloud migration, ERP implementations, and support for distribution, manufacturing, and service organizations.<ref>{{cite web |title=Innovia Consulting – Business Central Services |url=https://www.innovia.com |publisher=Innovia Consulting |access-date=2025-02-01}}</ref>

* '''Encore Business Solutions''' – A Canadian and U.S.-based Microsoft partner delivering Business Central, CRM, Power Platform, and Azure implementations across multiple industries.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dynamics 365 Business Central – Encore Business Solutions |url=https://www.encorebusiness.com |publisher=Encore Business Solutions |access-date=2025-02-01}}</ref>

* '''The NAV People (TNP)''' – A major UK-based partner known for Business Central/NAV training, support, and large-scale ERP deployments.<ref>{{cite web |title=TNP – The NAV/365 People |url=https://www.the365people.com |publisher=The NAV People |access-date=2025-02-01}}</ref>

These partners often supplement Business Central with industry-specific extensions, integrations, or custom development depending on customer requirements and local regulations.

==History==
'''Microsoft Dynamics''' was a line of Business Applications, containing [[enterprise resource planning]] (ERP) and [[customer relationship management]] (CRM). [[Microsoft]] marketed Dynamics applications through a network of reselling partners who provided specialized services.<ref name="Microsoft Dynamics ERP Partners">[http://www.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics/partner-information.aspx Microsoft Dynamics ERP]</ref> Microsoft Dynamics formed part of "Microsoft Business Solutions". Dynamics can be used with other Microsoft programs and services, such as [[SharePoint]], [[Yammer]], [[Office 365]], [[Microsoft Azure|Azure]] and [[Microsoft Outlook|Outlook]]. The Microsoft Dynamics focus-industries are retail, services, manufacturing, financial services, and the [[public sector]]. Microsoft Dynamics offers services for small, medium, and large businesses.<ref name=SMB>{{cite web|title= Small Business ERP: Microsoft Dynamics GP, NAV, SL|url= http://www.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics/erp-small-midsize-business.aspx|website= microsoft.com|publisher= Microsoft Dynamics|access-date= 8 September 2014}}</ref><ref name=Enterprise>{{cite web|title= Microsoft Business Solutions: CRM & ERP Enterprise Solutions|url= http://www.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics/enterprise-business-solutions.aspx|website= Microsoft Dynamics|access-date= 8 September 2014}}
</ref><ref>[http://social.technet.microsoft.com/wiki/contents/articles/34255.importance-of-microsoft-dynamics-erp-for-smbs.aspx TechNet Wiki: Importance of Microsoft Dynamics ERP for SMBs]</ref>

===Business Central===
'''Business Central''' was first published as '''Dynamics NAV''' and '''Navision''', which Microsoft acquired in 2002.

==== Navision====
Navision originated at PC&C A/S (Personal Computing and Consulting), a company founded in [[Denmark]] in 1984. PC&C released its first accounting package, [[PCPlus]], in 1985—a single-user application with basic accounting functionality. There followed in 1987 the first version of Navision,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dynamicsuser.net/wikis/navdev/the-history-of-dynamics-nav-navision.aspx|title=The history of Dynamics NAV/Navision|access-date=March 13, 2013|publisher=DynamicsUser.net|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140513013103/http://dynamicsuser.net/wikis/navdev/the-history-of-dynamics-nav-navision.aspx|archive-date=May 13, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> a [[client/server]]-based accounting application that allowed multiple users to access the system simultaneously. The success of the product prompted the company to rename itself to Navision Software A/S in 1995.

The Navision product sold primarily in Denmark until 1990. From Navision version 3 the product was distributed in other European countries, including Germany and the United Kingdom.

In 1995 the first version of Navision based on [[Microsoft Windows 95]] was released.

In 2000, Navision Software A/S merged with fellow Danish firm Damgaard A/S (founded 1983) to form NavisionDamgaard A/S.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.computerworld.dk/art/68766/damgaard-og-navision-i-storfusion|title=Damgaard and Navision in large merger (Danish)|date=20 November 2000 |access-date=March 13, 2013|publisher=Computerworld.dk}}</ref> In 2001 the company changed its name to "Navision A/S".

On July 11, 2002, Microsoft bought Navision A/S to go with its previous acquisition of [[Great Plains Software]]. Navision became a new division at Microsoft, named [[Microsoft Business Solutions]], which also handled [[Microsoft CRM]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.crn.com/it-channel/18828346 |title=It's Official: Microsoft buys Navision |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090202133133/http://www.crn.com/it-channel/18828346 |archive-date=2009-02-02}}</ref>

In 2003 Microsoft announced plans to develop an entirely new [[Enterprise resource planning|ERP]] system (Project Green). But it later decided to continue development of all ERP systems (Dynamics AX, Dynamics NAV, Dynamics GP and Dynamics SL). Microsoft launched all four ERP systems with the same new role-based user interface, [[SQL]]-based reporting and analysis, [[Microsoft SharePoint|SharePoint]]-based portal, [[Pocket PC]]-based mobile clients and integration with [[Microsoft Office]].

==== Dynamics NAV====
In September 2005, Microsoft re-branded the product and re-released it as Microsoft Dynamics NAV.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.microsoft.com/en-us/news/features/2005/sep05/09-06brand.aspx|title=Microsoft Introduces Microsoft Dynamics Brand|access-date=March 13, 2013|publisher=Microsoft}}</ref>

In December 2008, Microsoft released Dynamics NAV 2009, which contains both the original "classic" client, as well as a new [[.NET Framework]]-based [[three-tier]] [[graphical user interface|GUI]] called the RoleTailored Client (RTC).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/dd301204.aspx|title=What's New in Developing for Microsoft Dynamics NAV 2009|access-date=February 16, 2011|publisher=MSDN}}</ref>

In first quarter of 2014 NAV reached 102,000 current customers.<ref>{{cite web|title=How many companies use MS Dynamics|url=http://www.erpsoftwareblog.com/2014/03/how-many-companies-use-microsoft-dynamics-erp/|access-date=2 March 2014}}</ref>

In 2016, Microsoft announced the creation of [[Dynamics 365]] — a rebranding of the suite of Dynamics ERP and CRM products as a part of a new online-only offering.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/microsoft-readies-combined-crm-erp-dynamics-365-cloud-bundle/|title=Microsoft readies combined CRM, ERP Dynamics 365 cloud bundle|last=Foley|first=Mary Jo|publisher=ZDNet|date=July 6, 2016}}</ref> As a part of this suite, the successor to NAV was codenamed "Madeira".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/microsoft-takes-wraps-off-its-madeira-smb-business-management-service/|title=Microsoft takes wraps off its 'Madeira' SMB business-management service|last=Foley|first=Mary Jo|date=April 13, 2016|publisher=ZDNet}}</ref>

==== Dynamics 365 Business Central====
In September 2017 at the Directions conference, Microsoft announced the new codename 
"[[Tenerife]]" as the next generation of the Dynamics NAV product.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://msdynamicsworld.com/story/updated-dynamics-365-tenerife-release-plan-microsoft-aims-unify-nav-cloud-smb-erp|title=With updated Dynamics 365 "Tenerife" release plan, Microsoft aims to unify NAV, cloud SMB ERP|date=September 17, 2017|last=Gumpert|first=Jason|publisher=MSDynamicsWorld}}</ref> This replaced codename "Madeira".

On April 2, 2018, Business Central was released publicly<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Microsoft|title=Dynamics 365 Business Central is now live!date=April 2, 2018| date=2 April 2018 |url=https://cloudblogs.microsoft.com/dynamics365/no-audience/2018/04/02/dynamics-365-business-central-is-now-live/}}</ref> and plans for semi-annual releases were announced.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/microsofts-plan-to-put-dynamics-365-crmerp-on-a-twice-yearly-update-schedule/|title=Microsoft's plan to put Dynamics 365 CRM/ERP on a twice-yearly update schedule|date=July 6, 2018|publisher=ZDNet|last=Foley|first=Mary Jo}}</ref>

Business Central introduced a new [[AL language]] for development and translated the codebase from Dynamics NAV ([[C/AL]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/business-applications-release-notes/october18/dynamics365-business-central/business-central-everywhere|title=Business Central everywhere|date=September 12, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://msdynamicsworld.com/story/mastering-new-methods-dynamics-365-business-central-success|title=Mastering new methods for Dynamics 365 Business Central success|date=October 25, 2018|last=Demiliani|first=Stefano}}</ref>

=== Dynamics SL, Dynamics GP, Dynamics C5===
Several variants of the Dynamics brand have migration paths to Business Central with most having not had a new release since 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Using the C5 Data Migration Extension – Business Central|url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-au/dynamics365/business-central/ui-extensions-c5-data-migration|access-date=2022-02-24|website=docs.microsoft.com|language=en-au}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Cloud Migration Extensions – Business Central|url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/ui-extensions-data-replication|access-date=2022-02-24|website=docs.microsoft.com|language=en-us}}</ref> The later releases of the SL, GP, and C5 products adopted the Dynamics NAV Role-Tailored Client UI which helped pave the transition to the Business Central product.

==== History of Dynamics C5====
Dynamics C5 was developed in Denmark as the successor to the DOS-based Concorde C4. The developing company Damgaard Data merged with Navision in 2001 which was subsequently acquired by Microsoft Microsoft in 2002 rebranding the solution from Navision C5 to Microsoft Dynamics C5.<ref>{{Cite web|title=From Dynamics C5 to NAV|url=https://www.activebs.com/en/dynamics-erp/dynamics-c5|access-date=2022-02-24|website=www.activebs.com}}</ref>

The product handles currently more than 70,000 installations in Denmark.

==== History of Dynamics SL====
[[Image:Dynamics SL Connector.jpg|thumb|right|275px|Microsoft Dynamics SL Connector]]
Based in Findlay, Ohio, Solomon's roots go back more than 35 years, when co-founders Gary Harpst, Jack Ridge and Vernon Strong started TLB, Inc. in 1980. TLB, Inc. stands for The Lord's Business, "to remind the founders why the business was started: to conduct the business according to biblical principles." TLB was later renamed Solomon Software, and then Microsoft Dynamics SL.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.solomoncloudsolutions.com/solomon-software-history.html|title=Solomon Cloud Solutions, formerly Solomon Software, has a rich heritage dating back to 1980.|website=Solomon Cloud Solutions}}</ref>

==== History of Dynamics GP====
The Dynamics GP product was originally developed by [[Great Plains Software]], an independent company located in [[Fargo, North Dakota]] run by [[Doug Burgum]]. Dynamics Release 1.0 was released in February 1993.<ref name="msdn.com">{{cite web|url=http://blogs.msdn.com/b/developingfordynamicsgp/archive/2009/03/13/great-plains-historical-timeline.aspx|title=Great Plains Historical Timeline|work=msdn.com|access-date=29 December 2016}}</ref> It was one of the first accounting packages in the United States that were designed and written to be multi-user and to run under Windows as 32-bit software.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m0EIN/is_1995_Nov_13/ai_17591960?tag=content-inner;col1|title=FindArticles.com – CBSi|work=findarticles.com|access-date=29 December 2016}}</ref> In late 2000, [[Microsoft]] announced the purchase of Great Plains Software.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.techrepublic.com/article/why-microsoft-bought-great-plains-software/1053825/|title=Why Microsoft bought Great Plains Software – Page 1053825 – TechRepublic|work=techrepublic.com|date=11 January 2001 |access-date=29 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dynamicssquare.co.uk/products/dynamics-365-business-central/|title=Business Central – Advantages & Capabilities}}</ref> This acquisition was completed in April 2001.

Dynamics GP is written in a language called [[Dexterity (programming language)|Dexterity]]. Previous versions were compatible with [[Microsoft SQL Server]], [[Pervasive PSQL]], [[Btrieve]], and earlier versions also used [[C-tree]], although after the buyout all new versions switched entirely to Microsoft SQL Server databases.

Dynamics GP will no longer be updated after September 2029, with security updates through April 2031.<ref>{{cite web | title=Welcome to Dynamics GP | website=Microsoft Learn | date=2025-06-05 | url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics-gp/ | access-date=2025-09-05}}</ref>

===Finance===
'''Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance''' is a [[Microsoft]] [[enterprise resource planning]] (ERP) system for medium to large organizations. The software, part of the Dynamics 365 product line, was first on general release in November 2016, initially branded as '''Dynamics 365 for Operations'''. In July 2017, it was rebranded to '''Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations'''. At the same time, Microsoft rebranded their business software suite for small businesses (Business Edition, Financials) to '''Finance and Operations, Business Edition''', however, the two applications are based on completely different platforms. Its history includes:
* 1998 (March) – Axapta, a collaboration between [[IBM]] and Danish Damgaard Data, released in the Danish and US markets.
* 2000 – Damgaard Data merged with Navision Software A/S to form NavisionDamgaard, later named [[Navision]] A/S. Released Axapta 2.5. IBM returned all rights in the product to Damgaard Data shortly after the release of Version 1.5.
* 2002 – Microsoft acquires [[Navision]] A/S.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.microsoft.com/2002/07/11/microsoft-acquires-navision/|title=Microsoft Acquires Navision (2002)|date=11 July 2002 }}</ref> Released Axapta 3.0.
* 2006 – Released Microsoft Dynamics AX 4.0.
* 2008 – Released Microsoft Dynamics AX 2009.
* 2011 – Released Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.microsoft.com/en-us/news/press/2011/sep11/09-08DynamicsAX2012PR.aspx|title=Microsoft Dynamics AX 2012 Launches Worldwide|website=[[Microsoft]] |access-date=8 May 2018}}</ref> It was made available and supported in more than 30 countries and 25 languages. Dynamics AX is used in over 20,000 organizations of all sizes, worldwide.<ref>[https://www.randgroup.com/insights/what-is-microsoft-dynamics-ax/ What is Microsoft Dynamics AX?], randgroup.com</ref>
* 2016 – Released [[Microsoft Dynamics AX]] 7. Later rebranded to Dynamics 365 for Operations. This update was a major revision with a completely new UI delivered through a browser-based HTML5 client, and initially only available as a cloud-hosted application. This version lasted only a few months, though, as Dynamics AX was rebranded Microsoft Dynamics 365 for Operations in October 2016, and once more as [[Microsoft Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations|Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations]] in July 2017.
* 2017 – Rebranded to Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations, Enterprise Edition<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://msdynamicsworld.com/story/microsoft-introduce-dynamics-365-enterprise-plan-unified-operations-including-retail-talent|title=Microsoft to introduce Dynamics 365 enterprise plan for 'Unified Operations' including Retail, Talent|website=msdynamicsworld.com|date=10 May 2017 |language=en|access-date=2017-06-27}}</ref> (not to be mistaken with Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations Business Edition, which is based on former [[Microsoft Dynamics NAV]]).
* 2018 – Rebranded to Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations
* 2018 – The Human Resources Module became Dynamics 365 for Talent, now Dynamics 365 Human Resources. 
* 2020 – Rebranded and split into two products:<ref>{{Cite web|last=Corporation|first=Microsoft|title=Changes to Finance and Operations {{!}} Microsoft Dynamics 365|url=https://dynamics.microsoft.com/en-au/finance-and-operations-to-finance-and-scm/|access-date=2020-06-15|website=dynamics.microsoft.com|language=en}}</ref> 
** Dynamics 365 Finance
** Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
* 2023 – Dynamics 365 Human Resources re-integrated

===Sales===
[[File:Microsoft dynamics crm logo.png|thumb|Old ''Microsoft Dynamics CRM'' logo]]
'''Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales''' has undergone several iterations over its history. 

==== Microsoft CRM 1.2====
Microsoft CRM 1.2 was released on December 8, 2003.<ref>[http://www.microsoft.com/presspass/press/2003/dec03/12-08CRM12USLaunchPR.mspx "Enhanced Microsoft Business Solutions CRM 1.2 Is Available in North America"] ''Microsoft website''</ref> Microsoft CRM 1.2 was not widely adopted by industry.<ref>{{cite web|title=Beginners Guide to MB2-717 Exam – MB2-717 Exam Dumps Questions Answers|url=https://gallery.technet.microsoft.com/Beginners-Guide-to-MB2-717-1fb54504|access-date= 7 Aug 2018}}</ref> 

It was not possible to create custom entities but there was a [[software development kit]] (SDK) available using SOAP and [[XML]] endpoints to interact with it.

==== Microsoft Dynamics CRM 3.0====
The second version was rebranded as Microsoft Dynamics 3.0 (version 2.0 was skipped entirely) to signify its inclusion within the Dynamics product family and was released on December 5, 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.microsoft.com/presspass/press/2005/dec05/12-05CRM30UmbrellaPR.mspx |title=Microsoft Announces General Availability of Microsoft Dynamics CRM 3.0 |publisher=Microsoft.com |access-date=2011-12-22}}</ref>
Notable updates over version 1.2 are the ease of creating customizations to CRM, the switch from using [[Crystal Reports]] to [[Microsoft SQL Reporting Services]], and the ability to run on [[Windows Vista]] and [[Outlook 2007]]. 

Significant additions released later by Microsoft also allowed Dynamics CRM 3.0 to be accessed by various [[mobile device]]s and integration with [[Siebel Systems]]. This was the first version that saw reasonable take up by customers. 

You could create custom entities and (1xN) relations between the system/custom entities.

==== Microsoft Dynamics CRM 4.0====
Dynamics CRM 4.0 (a.k.a. Titan) was introduced in December 2007 (RTM build number 4.0.7333.3 Microsoft CRM build numbers from version 4.0 to version 8). It features multi-tenancy, improved reporting security, data importing, direct mail merging and support for newer technologies such as [[Windows Server 2008]]<ref>[http://support.microsoft.com/kb/950100 "Support for Microsoft Dynamics CRM 4.0 on Windows Server 2008-based computers"] ''Microsoft Website''</ref> and [[SQL Server 2008]] (Update Rollup 4).<ref>[http://support.microsoft.com/kb/957053 "Support for running Microsoft Dynamics CRM 4.0 together with Microsoft SQL Server 2008"] ''Microsoft Website''</ref>

Dynamics CRM 4.0 also implements CRM Online, a hosted solution{{solution-inline|date=July 2019}} that is offered directly by Microsoft. The multi-tenancy option also allows [[Independent software vendor|ISVs]] to offer hosted solutions{{solution-inline|date=July 2019}} to end customers as well.

Dynamics CRM 4.0 is the first version of the product, which has seen significant take up in the market and passed the 1 million user mark in July 2009.<ref>[http://www.microsoft.com/presspass/press/2009/jul09/07-13xRMInitiativePR.mspx "Microsoft Dynamics CRM Passes 1 Million User Mark and Expands xRM Initiative"] ''Microsoft Website''</ref>

Additional support for NxN relations was added, which solved a lot of 'in-between' entities. "Connections" were also introduced in favour of "Relations". The UI design was based on Office 2007 look and feel, with the same blue shading and round button as "start".

==== Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2011====
Dynamics CRM 2011 was released to open Beta in February 2010. It then went into Release Candidate stage in December 2010. The product was then released in February 2011 (build number 5.0.9688.583)

Browsers such as [[Internet Explorer]], [[Google Chrome|Chrome]] and [[Firefox]] browsers are fully supported since Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2011 Update Rollup 12.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://support.microsoft.com/kb/2784954|title=Browser compatibility introduced with Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2011 Update Rollup 12 and later versions |publisher=microsoft.com |access-date=2014-01-10}}</ref> Because of this browser compatibility R12 was highly anticipated but also caused a lot of stress for customers that had used unsupported customizations. R12 broke those customizations and clients had to rethink their changes. Microsoft offered additional wizards to pinpoint the problems.

==== Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2013====
Dynamics CRM 2013 was released to a closed beta group on July 28, 2013. Dynamics CRM 2013 Online went live for new signups in October 2013. It was released in November 2013 (build number 6.0.0000.0809).

==== Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2015====
On September 16, 2014, Microsoft announced that Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2015, as well as updates to its Microsoft Dynamics CRM Online and Microsoft Dynamics Marketing services, will be generally available in the fourth quarter of 2014. Microsoft also released a preview guide with details.

On November 30, 2014, Microsoft announced the general availability of Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2015 and the 2015 Update of Microsoft Dynamics Marketing.<ref>[https://community.dynamics.com/b/msftdynamicsblog/archive/2014/11/30/ringing-in-the-holidays-with-crm-2015.aspx?WT.mc_id=CIC_TWITTER_Community_20141203_%25click_time%25_117936032_MSFTDynamics&linkId=10964452 "Ringing in the holidays with CRM 2015"] ''Microsoft website''</ref>

On January 6, 2015, Microsoft announced the availability of a CRM Cloud service specifically for the [[US Government]] that is designed for [[FedRAMP]] compliance.<ref>[http://www.microsoft.com/en-us/government/blogs/microsoft-dynamics-crm-online-government-now-generally-available-to-all-us-government-customers/default.aspx#fbid=z57Gqa2BY8d "Microsoft Dynamics CRM Online Government Now Generally Available to All U.S. Government Customers"] ''Microsoft website''</ref>

==== Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2016====
Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2016 was officially released on November 30, 2015.<ref name="CRM 2015 PR">{{cite news|title=New Microsoft Dynamics CRM breaks down silos between marketing and sales|url=http://www.microsoft.com/en-us/news/press/2014/sep14/09-16crmpr.aspx?WT.mc_id=CIC_TWITTER_Product%20Feature_20140916_%25click_time%25_89008567_MSFTDynamics&linkId=9638285|access-date=22 September 2014|work=Microsoft|publisher=Waggener Edstrom Worldwide|date=16 September 2014}}</ref> Versions for CRM 2016 was 8.0, 8.1 and 8.2. With version 8.2 the name, Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2016, was changed to Dynamics 365

Microsoft Dynamics CRM 2016 was officially released on November 30, 2015. It includes advancements in intelligence, mobility and service, with significant productivity enhancements.<ref>[http://www.crmsoftwareblog.com/2015/09/microsoft-dynamics-crm-2016-release-date-announced-2/] ''CRM Software Blog''</ref> In June 2016 was developed a special application which sends scanned info from business cards into MS Dynamics CRM named Business Card Reader for MS Dynamics and Call Tracker application in 2017.

==== Microsoft Dynamics 365 sales====
Microsoft Dynamics 365 was officially released on November 1, 2016, as the successor to Dynamics CRM.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://searchcrm.techtarget.com/news/450300182/New-Microsoft-Dynamics-365-service-marries-CRM-to-ERP|title=New Microsoft Dynamics 365 service marries CRM to ERP|work=SearchCRM |publisher=TechTarget}}</ref> The product combines Microsoft business products (CRM and ERP Dynamics AX). A [[softphone]] dialer can be added as an extension.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/sales/sample-softphone-integration | title=Integrate sample softphone with Dynamics 365 Sales }}</ref>

The on-premises application, called Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement contained the following applications:
* Dynamics 365 for Sales 
* Dynamics 365 for Customer Service
* Dynamics 365 for Marketing
* Dynamics 365 for Field Service
* Dynamics 365 for Project Service Automation

The offerings Dynamics 365 for Finance and Operations cover the ERP needs, such as bookkeeping, invoice and order handling and manufacturing.

In Dynamics 365 version 9.0.0.1 many notable features like Virtual entities in Dynamics 365,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-04-29|title=Virtual Entity in Dynamics 365 V9.0 New Features|url=https://www.dynamixacademy.com/virtual-entity-in-dynamics-365/|access-date=2020-06-15|website=Dynamix Academy|language=en-US}}</ref> Auto Numbering Attributes, Multi Select Options sets etc. were introduced.

== Product updates==

=== October 2018 update===
The update released in October 2018 included new features for sales, marketing, customer service, and recruitment.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Foley|first=Mary Jo|title=Microsoft previews what's coming in Dynamics 365 this October|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/microsoft-previews-whats-coming-in-dynamics-365-this-october/|access-date=2021-07-19|website=ZDNet|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The Microsoft Dynamics 365 Update to 'One Version' and Why You Should Care|url=https://www.hso.com/innovation/news/the-microsoft-dynamics-365-update-to-one-version-and-why-you-should-care/|access-date=2021-07-19|website=HSO Innovation|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== April 2019 update===
This update was released on April 5, 2019. The features added after the update, included a user interface (UUI) to embed canvas apps created in PowerApps and it also brought back the tabs facility. The update also led to the removal of the Xrm.Page.data.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Microsoft Dynamics 365 April 2019 update: Was that v10?|url=https://www.chorus.co/resources/news/microsoft-dynamics-365-april-2019-update-was-that-v10|access-date=2021-07-19|website=www.chorus.co|language=en}}</ref>

=== February 2020 update===
An update was announced on February 19, 2019. The update included additions to the Customer Insights, Microsoft's customer data platform (CDP) such as new first and third-party data connections. In addition to this, this update brought forth new sales forecasting tools and Dynamics 365 Sales Engagement Center. The Dynamics 365 Project Operations was introduced in this update.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Microsoft Dynamics 365 update is focused on harnessing data|url=https://techcrunch.com/2020/02/19/microsoft-dynamics-365-update-is-focused-on-harnessing-data/|access-date=2021-07-19|website=TechCrunch|date=19 February 2020 |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== October 2021 update (wave 1)===
An update was announced on October 5, 2019. This update included a replacement of bank reconciliation reports. The payment reconciliation journal was improved to support preview posting, separate number series, and user-defined document numbers. Microsoft Dynamics 365 also welcomes Correct Dimensions action. With this update, Microsoft Dynamics 365 has welcomed integration with Microsoft Teams search box, Microsoft Word, and Microsoft Universal Print technology.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-03-02|title=Universal Print is ready for business|url=https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/windows-it-pro-blog/universal-print-is-ready-for-business/ba-p/2176778|access-date=2021-09-09|website=TECHCOMMUNITY.MICROSOFT.COM|language=en}}</ref>{{Citation needed|date=July 2021}}

==Related products==
Microsoft Dynamics includes a set of related products:

* Microsoft Dynamics Management Reporter. Management Reporter is a financial reporting and analysis application. Its main feature is to create income statements, balance sheet statements, cash flow statements and other financial reports. Reports can be stored in a centralized Report Library along with external supporting files. Security on reports and files may be controlled using Windows Authentication and SQL Server.
* Microsoft Dynamics for Retail (formerly Microsoft Dynamics RMS, QuickSell 2000 and Dynamics POS)
* Microsoft Dynamics for Marketing (formerly MDM and MarketingPilot 2012)
* Microsoft Dynamics Social Listening (formerly Netbreeze 2013)
* [[Power Automate]], formerly Microsoft Flow (until 2019<ref>[https://www.onmsft.com/news/ignite-2019-microsoft-flow-renamed-power-automate-adds-new-capabilities Ignite 2019: Microsoft Flow renamed "Power Automate," adds new capabilities – OnMSFT.com]</ref>), a toolkit similar to [[IFTTT]] for implementing business workflow products.
* Power Automate Desktop, [[robotic process automation]] software for automating graphical user interfaces (acquired in May 2020)<ref>[https://flow.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/microsoft-acquires-softomotive-to-expand-low-code-robotic-process-automation-capabilities-in-microsoft-power-automate/ Microsoft acquires Softomotive to expand low-code robotic process automation capabilities in Microsoft Power Automate]</ref>
* Parature customer engagement software in the customer support and service channels (acquired in January 2014)<ref>[https://techcrunch.com/2014/01/06/microsoft-acquires-parature-for-100m-in-deal-to-bolster-knowledge-base-for-dynamics-crm-platform/ Microsoft Acquires Parature For $100M In Deal To Bolster Knowledge Base For Dynamics CRM Platform]</ref>

Microsoft also sells Sure Step as an implementation methodology for Microsoft Dynamics for its re-sellers.

In July 2018, Microsoft announced Dynamics 365 AI for sales applications.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/microsoft-previews-whats-coming-in-dynamics-365-this-october/|title=Microsoft previews what's coming in Dynamics 365 this October|last=Foley|first=Mary Jo|work=ZDNet|access-date=2018-07-24|language=en}}</ref>
